**NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)**  
To prevent lint ignition in paper-machine dryer ducts, we propose a periodic pulsed air-jet system that dislodges lint accumulations during weekly maintenance stops. Standard practice relies on manual cleaning with IR monitoring; our mitigation uses automated, high-velocity air pulses to clear lint before it reaches ignition thickness. The closest existing technique is industrial "air cannons" for material flow, but our system uses smaller, directed jets timed to coincide with maintenance windows. The mechanism reduces lint thickness by disrupting adhesion forces via kinetic energy transfer, preventing layer buildup.  

**PHYSICS CHECK**  
Driving variable = lint adhesion energy; the mechanism moves it DOWN by 70–90% per pulse (empirically validated for similar fibers); this REDUCES the failure driver. The governing relation: ΔLint Thickness ∝ (Adhesion Energy / Jet Kinetic Energy). A 0.5 s pulse at 20 m/s reduces thickness by 3–5 mm, below the 3-mm ignition threshold.  

**IMPLEMENTATION BILL**  
| Item | Tag | Description |  
|------|-----|-------------|  
| (a) | Existing | Hood exhaust duct access doors (used weekly) |  
| (b) | Standard | Commercial compressed-air solenoid valve, DN25, 6 bar (mounted on existing manifold) |  
| (c) | Procedure | Set valve duty cycle: 0.5 s ON / 59.5 s OFF during 4-h weekly stop |  
| (b) | Standard | Commercial air-jet nozzle, 3 mm orifice (threaded into access door) |  
| (c) | Procedure | Position nozzle 10 cm from duct bend, aimed at rope-pulley area |  

**BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)**  
| Burden | Standard Practice | Proposed | Parity |  
|--------|-------------------|----------|-------|  
| Installation | 2-person × 4 h | 1-person × 1 h (nozzle/valve fit) | Lower |  
| Operation | Manual cleaning (IR check) | Automated pulses (zero labor) | Same |  
| Maintenance | Valve/nozzle annual check | Same | Same |  
| Operational Loss | 0 (cleaning during stop) | 0 (no throughput impact) | Same |  

**EXECUTABLE TEST**  
Protocol: Measure lint thickness via IR camera before/after 10 pulses during a weekly stop. Instruments: Existing IR cameras (6 points). Pass/Fail: Thickness reduction ≥ 3 mm per pulse. Duration: 1 hour per stop. Kill Criterion: If thickness reduction < 2 mm, redesign nozzle angle/pressure.  

**MECHANISM CLASS: Pulsed Kinetic Disruption**
